html:
On 17 August 1795 enslaved people on Curacao rose against their Dutch masters, led by a man named Tula. Up to a thousand people joined the revolt in the west of the island.

Tula had heard of the Haitian Revolution and of the French conquest of the Netherlands, which seemed to promise liberty. He demanded freedom, saying, "We seek only our freedom."

The Dutch put down the revolt within weeks. Tula and other leaders were tortured and executed in October. Slavery in the Dutch colonies lasted until 1863. Today 17 August is a day of remembrance on Curacao, and Tula is a national hero, alongside the story of Willemstad and the slave trade it served.
